rows.brief: Researchers reconstructed the May 2025 Blatten rock-and-ice avalanche using seismic recordings, terrain measurements and flow simulations. The study constrains the collapse dynamics and unusually low effective friction, but cannot uniquely identify the weakening mechanism. It is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated early-warning system.

rows.brief: ETH Zurich and IBM agreed to install and operate an IBM Quantum System Two with a Nighthawk processor at CSCS in Lugano. The three-year arrangement will provide access for Swiss research and selected companies. Operation was expected by the end of 2026; the announcement did not describe an already operational Zurich installation.

rows.brief: Colt announced commercial SCION connectivity for enterprises across Europe, North America and Asia after a two-year proof of concept with Anapaya. The service lets customers specify and audit network paths. This is a commercial deployment milestone, not the invention of SCION or a claim that all Colt traffic uses it.

rows.brief: Climeworks began capturing CO2 at Mammoth in Iceland in May 2024, with 12 of the planned 72 collector containers installed. The facility uses geothermal energy and Carbfix storage in basalt. Its announced 36,000-tonne annual nameplate capacity was a design target, not measured annual removal.

rows.brief: Taiho agreed to acquire Araris Biotech for $400 million at closing plus up to $740 million in development milestones. The deal brings Araris's AraLinQ antibody-drug conjugate platform and three preclinical candidates into Taiho. The headline $1.14 billion includes contingent payments, not cash paid upfront or evidence of clinical success.

rows.brief: Johnson & Johnson agreed to buy Numab's Yellow Jersey Therapeutics subsidiary for $1.25 billion in cash, securing global rights to NM26. The investigational bispecific antibody targets IL-4R alpha and IL-31 for atopic dermatitis and was ready to enter Phase 2. The transaction was not an acquisition of all Numab or proof of clinical efficacy.

rows.brief: Destinus signed an agreement to acquire Zurich-based Daedalean for CHF 180 million in cash and stock. Daedalean develops AI-based visual navigation and pilot-assistance systems for aviation. Completion was expected by the end of 2025; the announcement itself did not establish that the deal had closed or that its systems were certified.

rows.brief: ETH Zurich, EPFL and CSCS released Apertus in 8-billion- and 70-billion-parameter versions, with model weights, training code and documentation openly available. Trained on Alps using 15 trillion tokens across more than 1,000 languages, it is a foundation model for adaptation and deployment, not a finished consumer chatbot.
